key_insight: Learned smoothing improves energy-norm accuracy at a fixed multigrid budget, but larger classical smoothing budgets close the gap without a measured CPU advantage for learning.
engineering_relevance: For high-contrast elliptic finite element solves, fixed-budget accuracy gains should be weighed against runtime and robustness before adopting learned smoothers.
method: Train only the smoothers within an operator-adapted multigrid V-cycle.
Use operator-dependent transfers, Galerkin coarse operators, near-kernel deflation and an energy-norm safeguard.
Represent a specified class of fixed polynomial smoothers while preserving positive homogeneity in the load.
evidence_signal: On fresh problems, one learned pass reduced energy error by factors of 5.7–6.1 for conductive channels and 1.38–1.45 for insulating barriers versus the same cycle with four-step Jacobi-preconditioned CG smoothing; classical accuracy crossed the learned cycle at 8–14 and 5–8 steps per smoothing call, respectively.
watch_item: The tested CPU implementation showed no computational advantage over classical solvers, while load changes and floating islands further limited accuracy.
paper_title: Learned smoothing in operator-adapted multigrid: controlled accuracy gains and computational limits
